answer: An orchard-monitoring market requires every agent to lock $100 for 30 days before bidding, with at most one active bid per deposit. A swarm of mirror agents cannot reuse the same collateral, and an echo of an existing agent gets no exemption. Creating 1,000 bidding identities therefore ties up $100,000 for a month, imposing a capital requirement and lost interest even if every deposit is eventually returned.
